From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
Michelle GassBorn1968 (age 57–58)Maine, United StatesEducationWorcester Polytechnic Institute (BS)University of Washington (MBA)TitleCEO of Levi Strauss & Co.Spouse
Scott Gass​(m. 1994)​Children2
Michelle D. Gass (nee Petkers, born 1968)[1][2] is an American businesswoman who is the CEO of Levi Strauss & Co.[3] She previously was CEO of department store Kohl's.[4]
Education and career[edit]
Gass earned a bachelor's degree in chemical engineering from Worcester Polytechnic Institute in 1990[5][6] and an MBA from the University of Washington.[7]
She joined consumer goods company Procter and Gamble in 1990, where she worked in product development, before moving to Starbucks in 1996 as manager of its Frappuccino blended iced coffee brand.[8] At Starbucks, she was credited with turning Frappuccino into a $2 billion business, and her other company work included growing the company's Seattle's Best brand, now owned by Nestlé, and later led the retailer's expansion in Europe as Starbucks' EMEA president.[9]
In 2013, Gass joined department store Kohl's as chief customer officer, and in 2015 became the company's chief merchandising and customer officer.[10] In 2017, she was promoted to CEO-elect.[11] In May 2018, Gass officially became Kohl's CEO.[10] In 2018, Gass was named to Fortune magazine's list of most powerful women.[12] She was also named to Fortune's 2018 Businesssperson of the Year list.[13] In 2019, the National Retail Federation named Gass as the recipient of its Visionary 2020 award, awarded to the nation's top retail executive.[14] In 2019, Gass was elected to the board of directors of PepsiCo.[15]
In November 2022, it was announced that Gass would be stepping down as Kohl's CEO by early December to become the CEO-in-waiting for Levi Strauss & Co.[16] After one year as president of the Levi’s brand, she became the CEO of Levi Strauss & Co. in early 2024.[3]
In May 2025, Gass delivered the undergraduate Commencement address at Worcester Polytechnic Institute, where she was granted an honorary doctorate.[17]
Gass is a member of The Business Council.[18]
Gass was born and raised in Lewiston Maine.[19][20] She married Scott Gass on August 20, 1994.[21] They have two children.[22]

She also spent over 16 years in leadership roles at Starbucks. She began her career with Procter & Gamble. She currently serves on the board of directors for PepsiCo and on the boards of the Retail Industry Leaders Associates and the National Retail Federation. Michelle Gass (President and Chief Executive Officer, Levi Strauss & Co.) — public LinkedIn post, activity 7110974740462243840, dated 2023-09-22T13:14:53Z by the page's embedded metadata. Verbatim post text:

We like to say that everyone has a Levi’s® story. So here is my latest.   
 
Last Saturday night at Levi’s® Stadium, our brand was at the center of culture when Ed Sheeran played in front of a record-breaking crowd. Before Ed stepped on stage, I was thrilled to surprise him with his first-ever Levi’s® denim trucker jacket. 
 
Thanks to the team who created and personalized Ed’s jacket. It was a perfect fit. #liveinlevis

documents.title: Phil W. — LinkedIn post on Michelle Gass's Levi's performance
documents.excerpt:
Phil W. — public LinkedIn post, activity 7448029459452071936, dated 2026-04-09T15:30:00Z by the page's embedded metadata. Verbatim post text:

Michelle Gass is just killing it at Levi Strauss, where she's been CEO for two years. Revenue rose 14% last quarter, and her strategy of selling more tops, more women's wear and more through Levi's own stores is clearly working. It's such a contrast to her struggles at Kohl's, which three CEOs later is still struggling. 

Same person, same skills, different performance. So what gives? (I ask because I remember many predicting doom for Levi's when it was announced she was joining the company, pointing to her Kohl's performance.)

In my CEO Daily column today, I explore that. Some CEOs are better suited for turnarounds (which require a very specific skillset) and others for expansion. Some might be in the right place at the right time and get too much credit for success, or, conversely, get blamed for being unable to fix an unfixable company. In Gass’s case, the seasoned executive has found a role that aligns with her particular set of retail chops, and for now, Levi’s is stronger for it.

Please read this in Fortune:
https://lnkd.in/eDePXWqK

unjustified.statement: Michelle Gass is the chief executive of Kohl's.
unjustified.why: She stepped down from Kohl's by early December 2022 and has led Levi Strauss & Co. since 2024. Public identity records that were not updated still describe her as Kohl's CEO.

unjustified.statement: She built Frappuccino into a two-billion-dollar business by herself.
unjustified.why: The source says she was credited with it. A credit is not a record of who did what, and a brand of that size is not one person's output.

unjustified.statement: She works as a chemical engineer.
unjustified.why: Her degree is in chemical engineering. Every retained record of her working life is in consumer goods and retail management.

unjustified.statement: Gass's #liveinlevis brand posts independently verify her performance as Levi's CEO.
unjustified.why: Her LinkedIn posts are self-reports of brand moments, not independent assessments; only third-party accounts such as Phil W.'s can verify performance claims.

unavailable.reason: No retained source records unsuccessful work or a postmortem.
No retained source documents a constraint environment she worked under.
No retained source follows the work she led at Kohl's after she left.
